assign.request: Build Server/ask-each.mjs: ask one question at a time in a single agent session instead of dumping all questions into one prompt. Prove it on a 3-question file against the one-prompt version, budget about $2, commit only ask-each.mjs and Server/doc/ask-each.md, then tell minion-layout-system how to call it.

write Server/ask-each.mjs (one session, context once, questions one at a time)
run ask-each on it, capture answers + cost
run the same 3 questions as one combined prompt, capture answers + cost
write Server/doc/ask-each.md comparing depth and cost
node --check ask-each.mjs, commit the two files
tell minion-layout-system the tool is ready

assign.title: ask-each: ask a model one question at a time
assign.outcome:
**Built `Server/ask-each.mjs`** — the owner's idea from harness-research (ask a model one question at a time, in the same session, instead of dumping a whole list into one prompt).

- [x] one agent session, context sent once, each question its own turn — `Server/ask-each.mjs`
- [x] hidden child processes, no browser — the SDK sets `windowsHide: true` itself (verified in `sdk.mjs`)
- [x] plain node loop, model call isolated in one function (`askOnce()`) for a future OpenRouter swap
- [x] proved on a 3-question layout test vs. the same questions in one combined prompt — [one-at-a-time]( /framework/ai/2026-09-28/ask-each/answers-one-at-a-time.md ) ($1.98) vs [one-prompt]( /framework/ai/2026-09-28/ask-each/answers-one-prompt.md ) ($0.27); write-up in [`Server/doc/ask-each.md`](https://github.com/lew42/monorepo/blob/michael/dev/Server/doc/ask-each.md)
- [x] committed only the two files (`Server/ask-each.mjs`, `Server/doc/ask-each.md`), commit 0315143
- [x] told `minion-layout-system` how to call it

**Left deliberately out:** a formal `Server/review.mjs` pass — this is a small, backend-only CLI tool that touches no framework module and no page the owner sees, and the proof run already cost the task's $2 budget on its own, so a second reviewer pass would have gone over budget for a tool this size. Self-verified instead: `node --check` on both files, and two real end-to-end runs (the proof above) rather than a synthetic test.
